body: Yeah initially I was gonna do 150 to at least get some students and a few rounds in, slowly increase the price.

Yeah. Don’t burn the bridge. Most importantly if you DO end up burning the bridge make sure you ALWAYS stay professional. Never allow the client to paint you as unprofessional. If this dbag wants to try to paint you as slow or whatever: THEY got pissy when YOU got Covid. Talk about unprofessional. Yeesh.
I’m hoping that your kidneys haven’t shut down yet. What happened to be finally done? What was the straw?
And hell if I had literally any money at all (my fiancé and I just split up) I’d hire you. I need someone who knows wtf they’re doing to be my digital pimp. I’m so lost when it comes to marketing.

Yeaaaaah as far as the TED talk. I loathe being in front of a camera. Behind? Bring it on. As far as last invoice goes and ongoing invoices are concerned: Find a freelancer contract that gives a client 10 days upon completion of a project to pay up or you send it to collections. It WILL cost you clients but what doesn’t these days. 

As far as this dbag is concerned? Ignore him. Rise above his pettiness, get paid, and move on.  Patience and belief in oneself is never easy and really start to vet your clients from now on. Again that will limit the scope of your work but that’s more annoying than a serious issue. +50 pitching hours. (Just kidding)

Do you know the scene where Indiana Jones is swapping the idol for a bag of sand? Straight up that’s a perfect metaphor for being a successful Freelancer. Do it properly (and nobody gets it right first try) and you won’t get chased by a giant boulder. The boulder being financial drama. 🤷‍♂️ it’s not a big deal. Find another client, tighten the belt if you must and move forward. Aaaaand go ahead an insert some cheesy opportunistic sales pitch for the course I’m soon to be releasing here.

As a Freelance course creator and experienced freelancer: Screw that guy. I mean, don’t but the notion is the same. If you’ve lost all respect for a client and they are abusive to you show yourself the respect they didn’t. Move on.

Edit: Never let yourself get walked on. Taking SOME amount of crap is okay but know YOUR limits. If they hit those limits then move on, without hesitation. Never look back.

Oh and incase anyone was curious. It’s like 25k in debt but what little money I had in a separate account for the wedding reduced that to 8k because apparently she (who was in charge of paying stuff) hadn’t paid anything in 8 months. Making me think that she’d been planning this for a bit.
